title: Who Decides and Who Does? | Principles of Management Ep 4
description:
Chai Corner now stays open sixteen hours a day, and Ravi cannot be there for all of it. When Asha and Kabir keep changing the price of chai, nobody knows who is in charge. The fix is to split two jobs that are often mixed up: administration and management.

In this animated lesson you will learn that administration decides the policies and goals (the thinking function), while management carries those policies out (the doing function). We compare the two row by row (level, function, focus, decisions and who does them), and look at the three classic views: Oliver Sheldon (administration above management), E.F.L. Brech (administration is a part of management), and modern writers like Harold Koontz (the two words mean the same thing).

This is Episode 4 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.

In this video:
0:00 Who is in charge at Chai Corner?
0:22 Administration vs management: thinking and doing
0:41 What is a policy?
0:52 Ravi decides, Meena does
1:05 Comparison table, row by row
1:36 Three views: Sheldon, Brech, Koontz
1:56 Quick check
2:07 Recap

Next episode: Levels of Management.
